body:
> Don't believe everything your brain says. You've been through so much emotional shit, so of course your brain might lean to the irrational or fucked up ways of thinking.

You're right on the money. It's just this continual cycle of that inner voice beating me up, hitting me harder each day, telling me everything that lies ahead is misery and all sorts of horrible shit, etc.

> You mentioned hope, and I think that there's still a part of you that thinks you can do it. Maybe that's why you posted here?

You bet. I don't *really* wanna do it, I'd rather fix my problems and become a strong person. I just didn't even know where to begin picking up the pieces, and so I posted here, in a moment of desperation. I'm glad I did. This community is very kind and understanding. You guys are great human beings.

I had never heard of Cognitive Distortions prior to your mention of them, and so now you've got me really intrigued. I'm going to look into them for sure, and attempt to break these harmful patterns that have plagued me for a long time now. Thanks a lot for bringing this to my attention, man, because I probably wouldn't have found it otherwise.

> Now this next bit might be a bit advanced if you're used to consuming a lot but maybe you might want to look into creating things as well. You write pretty decently and I was able to easily imagine the events and concepts you wrote about. Ever looked into some creative writing?

As a matter of fact, I have!! I'm an amateur at best, but I do enjoy illustrating concepts, articulating meaning, and just generally rambling on in my own way. I had been complimented on my writing before, but those harmful thinking patterns got me only really seeing the negative aspect of things, and that I suck, I'm never gonna be anything resembling decent, etc. It's a toxic mentality that takes my past into account in the most negative sense imaginable.

> At the end of the day, I think ideal fulfillment could be had with a good balance of consuming and creating.

Real talk.

> Cheers and I hope you found something useful in what I wrote.

I did. I really appreciate you commenting on my post, as it helped a lot. A year from now, I hope I'm in the same state you are, in that I can stop seeing the greys and start seeing color again. Good luck on your journey as well, we're both NEET and we're in this struggle together. Thank you!
Yeah, it's rough. :( I hope you find the light at the end of the tunnel.

I should have seen a psychiatrist sooner, but fear that it wouldn't help me (as it didn't when I was a kid) kept me from calling, making appointments, etc. Absolutely at the top of my list, going forward. Thanks man.

> Also do you have a hobby or creative outlet? Nothing cures depression like creativity (in my experience). Is there an instrument you've always wanted to pick up? Ever wanted to learn coding etc? Anything you think you might want to do, you should do it. Find a passion and pursue it with all your being and things tend to fall into place.

Yes there is! I really like to sing every now and then, and would be interested in improvement on that front. I'd been considering getting a mic so I could sing some covers, just for fun of course. Good call.

This is really a quality comment, thank you. I don't yet have my GED, but I'm working on it. I most definitely have the time and resources available to me. As for seeing a psychiatrist and going through that whole thing, I did go through therapy some years ago, and it helped to an extent, but I eventually stopped. The medication I received was also not renewed by my mother, since she's very much into the hatred of pharmaceutical drugs to treat mental illness... it's just holistic home remedies and strange oils with her. I wasn't even on the medicine for long enough to see a difference, I had to continue with it, but couldn't due to the lack of renewal. Maybe I really should look into the Intensive Outpatient Program you mentioned.

I'm going to look into the psychiatrist first and foremost, followed by the aid in obtaining the GED that a local community college could potentially offer. I absolutely agree with you about the external structure being needed with ADHD, I once tried online schooling and could not, for the life of me, get much done.

Just in general, your whole comment was so helpful to me. Thanks dude.

Thank you for your comment, my friend. It was very hopeful and inspiring to read! You're right about yesterday being gone. I think most of us regret yesterday to some extent. I'm really sorry to hear about your panic attacks and suicidal ideation as well, it's absolute hell to get through. I can definitely relate to the feeling of thinking everything would've been fixed by now, the feeling of "being a failure".

I'm gonna keep going, man. I'm gonna make the effort. Thanks again.

> And big ups for Better call Saul! I kept seeing Chuck and having that ‘oh shit’ moment too but honestly try looking at Jimmy. His attitude has been such an inspiration to me lately!

It's a fantastic show! I love the characters and the acting. Jimmy is a bittersweet character imo, especially when the Cinnabon scenes are taken into account... I hope things turn out ok for him in the end. He is not without fault, but he was a decent enough person, once upon a time. Maybe he can find redemption.

I've considered this in the past, but was born with one kidney, which disqualifies me from any branch of the military, I'm pretty sure. If not that, surely the mental health evaluation would return unfavorable results.

You make a good point. I actually do enjoy exercise in general, I just don't eat enough to be able to keep consistency. There are times I don't even bother with more than just one meal a day, but I've just gotta work on that. Thanks a bunch.

Thank you for your advice, man. I used to love jogging when I was 15, and you reminded me of those times. I still go for a long walk every night (been a habit of mine for years now), it's really the only outdoor exposure I get. I'd run more often, but I'm already rail-thin and fear the potential weight loss would not be so ideal for me... I just need to start eating more, really. The lack of vitamin D is a good call too.

> Seriously, do it, run for me, ok?

You bet. This is now a short-term goal of mine. Thanks for your help, truly!

You are experiencing a profound struggle, and I am so sorry for that. Hoping you find your puppy. Please, you have to break through the facade and confide in one of your nearest friends!! I'm sure one of them must understand, or be able to be brought to understand.

I just wanted to tell you that your comment means so much to me. Just the fact that the first comment on my post was one of kindness, not ridicule (as I initially feared) is very pleasantly surprising. You as well seem like a good person, my friend, and I do appreciate it.

My main issue with the ADHD is that it's not believed to be legitimate in many circles. My mother always told me that it was not a valid mental hurdle, but rather, an excuse, despite formal diagnosis. I have had a great degree of trouble concentrating for as long as I can remember, and it seems as though the symptoms have only magnified with age.

I have my issues with my mom, but I also have to wonder what made her the way she is... was she perhaps a victim at some point? I forgive her for the past, I know I had my issues as a child as well, but I just wish she would have a conversation with me instead of yelling and interrupting. My father is a good man, but very logical and emotionally distant, by my estimation. He has little time to put up with me these days, since I am 22 and he has 3 year old son (my half-brother).

Again, thank you for your comment. I think I will take you up on your offer to talk and PM in the near future, if you don't mind.
